intro.title: Build typed query string serializer
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed query string serializer—a function that converts a JavaScript object into a properly formatted URL query string (like `?name=John&age=25`). You will learn how to use TypeScript's type system to ensure the input object has string values, making your code safer and more predictable. The main technologies involved are TypeScript interfaces for defining object shapes and built-in methods like `Object.entries()` and `encodeURIComponent()` for string manipulation. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe utility that can be integrated into web applications.
intro.usecase: Typed query string serializers are essential in modern web applications that handle complex filtering and data navigation. You'll find them powering dashboard filtering systems in analytics tools like Google Analytics or Tableau, where users can save and share custom report views. They're also crucial in e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Shopify, enabling customers to refine product searches with multiple filters (price, category, rating) while maintaining shareable URLs. As a developer, implementing this pattern ensures your application's state is predictable, shareable, and type-safe when users interact with search interfaces, data tables, or any UI component that needs to persist state in the URL.
